title: Finite-stage domains for closed boundary duality
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are $k$-schemes. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], taken small in a larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. On either site $D^b_{ctf}$ denotes bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensoring with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A locally closed piece $W\subseteq Y$ is a subscheme given by an immersion into $Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Every such $W$ is separated and finite type over $k$ and is Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact). For its structure map $a_W$ the etale compact-support right adjoint $a_W^\times$ exists on the ambient derived categories and preserves $D^+$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Put $\omega_{W,e}=a_W^\times A$ and $D_{W,e}=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_{W,e})$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This duality preserves $D^b_{ctf}(W_e,A)$ and its evaluation double-dual morphism $\delta$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing] is invertible there.

For any closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between these pieces, let $G=i^\times$ be the ambient right adjoint of $Ri_!=Ri_*$ and $s=i_e^*$. Then $s$ and $G$ both carry $D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(Z_e,A)$. For $L\in D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$, put $P=sD_{T,e}L$ and $U=GL$. There is a natural costalk isomorphism $\widetilde\alpha_{D_{T,e}L}:GD_{T,e}D_{T,e}L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{Z,e}P$, and $\widetilde c_L=\widetilde\alpha_{D_{T,e}L}\circ G\delta_L:U\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{Z,e}P$. No evaluation normalization is asserted for $\widetilde\alpha$.

For $\tau=e,p$ write $\omega_{W,p}=Ra_{W,p}^!A$ and use the specified exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The mate of bounded-below compact-support composition gives counit-compatible identifications $Ri_\tau^!\omega_{T,\tau}\cong\omega_{Z,\tau}$. For $p$ this is on bounded-below etale-origin objects under $C_W=\nu_W^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], with $Ri_p^!=C_ZGR\nu_{T,*}$.

proof.text: Use Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace to make Y Noetherian. An immersion is a topological embedding, so IsInducing.noetherianSpace makes W a Noetherian topological space. Thus w is quasi-compact. Immersions are locally of finite type and separated, and composition with aY gives all three structure-map instances. The same finite-type argument makes W a Noetherian scheme. This avoids a separate open-closed factorization proof.

proof.text: Construct the natural costalk isomorphism in the ordinary constant-module categories directly. The proved verdierDualLowerShriekIso, applied to derivedHomRightDerivedLowerShriekIsoOfFinite and boundaryDualizingEtaleIso, identifies R i_! followed by DT.rightOp with DZ.rightOp followed by (R i_*).op. The self-adjunctions MonoidalClosed.ihomFlipSelfAdjunction and the ordinary derived pullback/direct-image adjunction identify the right adjoint of the latter composite with s.op followed by DZ. Conjugate this natural isomorphism with the ambient exceptional adjunction and DT self-adjunction to obtain alpha: DT followed by G is naturally isomorphic to s.op followed by DZ. This is a construction from proved source declarations; it does not choose unrelated component isomorphisms.

proof.text: For finite-Tor constructible L, G maps the canonical biduality isomorphism to an isomorphism. Compose it with alpha at DT L. The result is an isomorphism G L to DZ(s(DT L)). Steps 3 and 4 put the latter in the finite-Tor constructible category. Translate to the source predicate, apply prop_of_iso separately to boundedConstructible and finiteTorAmplitude using the inverse isomorphism, and translate back. This gives exceptional preservation and the remaining invertibility clause, and assembles all conjuncts of BoundaryClosedFiniteTorDomains and BoundaryPieceFiniteTorDomains.
